nodes.label: Optical disc image / ISO image
nodes.description: Disk image containing everything that would be written to an optical disc, sector by sector, including its optical-disc filesystem.

nodes.label: ISO image
nodes.description: Optical-disc image commonly associated with ISO 9660.

nodes.label: Disk image
nodes.description: General image representation of storage media.

nodes.label: Optical disc
nodes.description: Physical optical storage medium.

nodes.label: Logical sector
nodes.description: User-data portion of a data-optical-disc sector; the source gives 2,048 bytes.

nodes.label: Raw disc image
nodes.description: Raw representation containing complete disc information, including information from all tracks.

nodes.label: UDF
nodes.description: ISO/IEC 13346 filesystem commonly used by DVDs and Blu-ray Discs.

nodes.label: ISO image vs raw disc image
nodes.description: ISO stores logical-sector user data and omits control/error-correction information; raw images can retain complete disc information.

nodes.label: Filesystem vs physical track
nodes.description: A filesystem can reside inside a physical track, but ISO does not model physical tracks as track containers.

nodes.label: Data optical disc vs audio CD
nodes.description: Data discs use filesystem-bearing sectors; audio CDs use continuous encoded audio streams and track addressing.

nodes.label: Single-track vs multi-track
nodes.description: A single-track data disc can be represented as an ISO; a multi-track disc cannot be fully represented by one ISO.

nodes.label: ISO semantics vs .img extension
nodes.description: .img may be used for ISO images but can also denote images with different contents.

nodes.label: ISO 9660 vs UDF
nodes.description: Both filesystem structures can occur in optical-disc images; UDF is commonly associated with DVD/Blu-ray in the source.

nodes.label: Image vs physical disc
nodes.description: Image is a transferable binary artifact; physical disc is the optical medium it represents.

nodes.label: Mount vs burn
nodes.description: Mount exposes image through an OS interface; burning creates physical optical media.

nodes.label: Archival vs emulation
nodes.description: The same image artifact can preserve disc contents or provide input to an emulator.

nodes.label: ISO vs virtual CD-ROM
nodes.description: ISO is the stored image; virtual CD-ROM is the runtime interface exposing it as optical media.

nodes.label: Filesystem binary copy vs raw media copy
nodes.description: ISO preserves filesystem/user data rather than every physical-media control/error structure.

nodes.label: Track addressing vs file addressing
nodes.description: Audio CD content is addressed through track/index/time structures rather than filesystem files.

nodes.label: ISO image structure
nodes.description: optical_disc_image = ordered logical-sector user-data + filesystem structure

nodes.label: ISO size constraint
nodes.description: ISO_size = N × 2048 bytes

nodes.label: ISO creation pipeline
nodes.description: optical_disc → imaging software → ISO | file collection → authoring software → ISO

nodes.label: Mount model
nodes.description: ISO → mount driver → OS mount interface → filesystem/files

nodes.label: Burn model
nodes.description: ISO → burning tool → recordable optical disc

nodes.label: Multi-track limitation
nodes.description: complete_multi_track_disc ↛ single_ISO

nodes.label: Raw multi-track model
nodes.description: complete_disc + track metadata → raw image + companion descriptor

nodes.label: Audio CD model
nodes.description: audio track → continuous encoded stream → track/index/time addressing

nodes.label: Emulation model
nodes.description: ISO → emulator → emulated optical-disc contents

nodes.label: Virtual CD model
nodes.description: ISO → virtual CD-ROM → hypervisor/guest

nodes.label: USB image-writing model
nodes.description: raw image → image-writing software → USB flash drive

nodes.label: Archival transfer model
nodes.description: physical optical disc → image → data link/removable storage → destination

nodes.label: Definition
nodes.description: Optical disc image is a sector-by-sector disk image containing disc filesystem and data.

nodes.label: Creation
nodes.description: Images can be created from optical discs, file collections, or other image files.

nodes.label: Sector semantics
nodes.description: ISO stores user data, not control headers/error correction; logical data sectors are 2,048 bytes.

nodes.label: Transferability
nodes.description: An image can be transferred over data links/removable media unlike a physical optical disc.

nodes.label: Mounting
nodes.description: Suitable driver software can expose ISO to the OS as though it were a physical optical disc.

nodes.label: Multiple tracks
nodes.description: ISO has no physical track concept and cannot fully represent multi-track discs.

nodes.label: Audio CDs
nodes.description: Audio CDs cannot be represented as ISO because audio tracks contain continuous encoded audio rather than filesystems.

nodes.label: Raw formats
nodes.description: CUE/BIN, CCD/IMG, and MDS/MDF can store complete multi-track images with companion track metadata.

nodes.label: USB
nodes.description: Historically, writing ISO to flash drives was limited by software tooling; raw-image writers later existed.

nodes.label: Uses
nodes.description: ISO is used for emulation, virtual CD-ROMs for hypervisors, and OS installation media.

nodes.label: ISO is always a raw copy of every physical disc byte
nodes.description: False: source says ISO omits control headers and error-correction data.

nodes.label: Every optical disc can be stored in one ISO
nodes.description: False: multi-track and audio-disc structures exceed the ISO filesystem model.

nodes.label: An ISO contains physical tracks
nodes.description: False: source explicitly says there is no concept of a track inside an ISO.

nodes.label: Audio CD tracks are files
nodes.description: False: source describes continuous encoded audio rather than a filesystem.

nodes.label: .img always means exactly the same thing as .iso
nodes.description: False: .img can contain different kinds of image data.

nodes.label: UDF cannot occur in an ISO image
nodes.description: False: source explicitly says an ISO image may contain UDF.

nodes.label: Mounting an ISO burns it to a disc
nodes.description: False: mounting exposes it virtually; burning creates physical media.

nodes.label: ISO cannot be transferred because it represents physical media
nodes.description: False: image is a binary file and can move over links/removable storage.

nodes.label: USB limitations are inherent to ISO format
nodes.description: False: source attributes historical limitation to software-tool availability.

nodes.label: ISO and virtual CD-ROM are identical concepts
nodes.description: False: ISO is stored representation; virtual CD-ROM is runtime interface.

source_claims.text: Optical disc image is a sector-by-sector disk image containing disc filesystem and data.
Images can be created from optical discs, file collections, or other image files.
ISO stores user data, not control headers/error correction; logical data sectors are 2,048 bytes.
An image can be transferred over data links/removable media unlike a physical optical disc.
Suitable driver software can expose ISO to the OS as though it were a physical optical disc.
ISO has no physical track concept and cannot fully represent multi-track discs.
Audio CDs cannot be represented as ISO because audio tracks contain continuous encoded audio rather than filesystems.
CUE/BIN, CCD/IMG, and MDS/MDF can store complete multi-track images with companion track metadata.
Historically, writing ISO to flash drives was limited by software tooling; raw-image writers later existed.
ISO is used for emulation, virtual CD-ROMs for hypervisors, and OS installation media.

semantic_distinctions.label: ISO image vs raw disc image
semantic_distinctions.description: ISO stores logical-sector user data and omits control/error-correction information; raw images can retain complete disc information.

semantic_distinctions.label: Filesystem vs physical track
semantic_distinctions.description: A filesystem can reside inside a physical track, but ISO does not model physical tracks as track containers.

semantic_distinctions.label: Data optical disc vs audio CD
semantic_distinctions.description: Data discs use filesystem-bearing sectors; audio CDs use continuous encoded audio streams and track addressing.

semantic_distinctions.label: Single-track vs multi-track
semantic_distinctions.description: A single-track data disc can be represented as an ISO; a multi-track disc cannot be fully represented by one ISO.

semantic_distinctions.label: ISO semantics vs .img extension
semantic_distinctions.description: .img may be used for ISO images but can also denote images with different contents.

semantic_distinctions.label: ISO 9660 vs UDF
semantic_distinctions.description: Both filesystem structures can occur in optical-disc images; UDF is commonly associated with DVD/Blu-ray in the source.

semantic_distinctions.label: Image vs physical disc
semantic_distinctions.description: Image is a transferable binary artifact; physical disc is the optical medium it represents.

semantic_distinctions.label: Mount vs burn
semantic_distinctions.description: Mount exposes image through an OS interface; burning creates physical optical media.

semantic_distinctions.label: Archival vs emulation
semantic_distinctions.description: The same image artifact can preserve disc contents or provide input to an emulator.

semantic_distinctions.label: ISO vs virtual CD-ROM
semantic_distinctions.description: ISO is the stored image; virtual CD-ROM is the runtime interface exposing it as optical media.

semantic_distinctions.label: Filesystem binary copy vs raw media copy
semantic_distinctions.description: ISO preserves filesystem/user data rather than every physical-media control/error structure.

semantic_distinctions.label: Track addressing vs file addressing
semantic_distinctions.description: Audio CD content is addressed through track/index/time structures rather than filesystem files.

misconceptions_and_corrections.label: USB limitations are inherent to ISO format
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: False: source attributes historical limitation to software-tool availability.

misconceptions_and_corrections.label: ISO and virtual CD-ROM are identical concepts
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: False: ISO is stored representation; virtual CD-ROM is runtime interface.
